t: Imam al-Bukhari died in 256 AH.
f: Imam al-Bukhari died in 156 AH.
x: Al-Bukhari died in 256 AH.

t: Imam Muslim was a student of al-Bukhari.
f: Imam al-Bukhari was a student of Imam Muslim.
x: Muslim studied under al-Bukhari, who was older.

t: Abu Hanifah died in 150 AH.
f: Abu Hanifah died in 250 AH.
x: Abu Hanifah died in 150 AH, the year al-Shafi'i was born.

t: Malik ibn Anas compiled al-Muwatta'.
f: Ahmad ibn Hanbal compiled al-Muwatta'.
x: Malik compiled al-Muwatta'. Ahmad compiled the Musnad.

t: Al-Shafi'i studied under Malik.
f: Malik studied under al-Shafi'i.
x: Al-Shafi'i, the younger, studied the Muwatta' under Malik in Madinah.

t: Ahmad ibn Hanbal studied under al-Shafi'i.
f: Abu Hanifah studied under Ahmad ibn Hanbal.
x: Ahmad studied with al-Shafi'i. Abu Hanifah died before Ahmad was born.

t: Al-Shafi'i died in Egypt.
f: Al-Shafi'i died in Yemen.
x: Al-Shafi'i spent his last years in Egypt and died there in 204 AH.

t: Ahmad ibn Hanbal was persecuted in the Mihnah over the createdness of the Qur'an.
f: Ahmad ibn Hanbal was persecuted for refusing to pray Jumu'ah.
x: He refused to say the Qur'an was created and was imprisoned and flogged.

t: Ibn Kathir was a student of Ibn Taymiyyah.
f: Ibn Taymiyyah was a student of Ibn Kathir.
x: Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH) studied under Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728 AH).

t: Al-Nawawi compiled Riyad as-Salihin.
f: Ibn Hajar compiled Riyad as-Salihin.
x: Riyad as-Salihin is al-Nawawi's. Ibn Hajar wrote Bulugh al-Maram.

t: Ibn Hajar wrote Fath al-Bari on Sahih al-Bukhari.
f: Ibn Hajar wrote Fath al-Bari on Sahih Muslim.
x: Fath al-Bari explains Sahih al-Bukhari. Al-Nawawi's commentary is on Sahih Muslim.

t: Al-Tabari wrote both a tafsir and a history.
f: Al-Tabari wrote only books of poetry.
x: Al-Tabari wrote Jami' al-Bayan in tafsir and the History of the Prophets and Kings.

t: Ibn Hisham edited the Sirah of Ibn Ishaq.
f: Ibn Ishaq edited the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.
x: Ibn Ishaq wrote the earlier biography. Ibn Hisham edited it.

t: The six books of hadith include Sunan Ibn Majah.
f: The six books of hadith include Musnad Ahmad.
x: The six are al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah. The Musnad is not among them.

t: A mursal hadith omits the companion from the chain.
f: A mursal hadith is one narrated by a hundred companions.
x: In a mursal hadith a successor narrates directly from the Prophet ﷺ.

t: A mawquf report stops at a companion.
f: A mawquf report is raised to the Prophet ﷺ.
x: Mawquf stops at a companion. A report raised to the Prophet ﷺ is marfu'.

t: A hadith qudsi is narrated by the Prophet ﷺ from Allah.
f: A hadith qudsi is part of the Qur'an.
x: A hadith qudsi conveys Allah's words in the Prophet's narration, but it is not Qur'an.

t: Al-Tirmidhi often graded hadith as hasan in his Jami'.
f: Al-Tirmidhi never graded the hadith in his Jami'.
x: Al-Tirmidhi regularly comments on grades, often saying hasan or hasan sahih.

t: The Qur'an was gathered under Abu Bakr after many reciters died at Yamamah.
f: The Qur'an was gathered under Abu Bakr after many reciters died at Badr.
x: Umar urged Abu Bakr after many reciters were killed at Yamamah.

t: Hudhayfah urged Uthman to unify the copies of the Qur'an.
f: Khalid ibn al-Walid urged Uthman to unify the copies of the Qur'an.
x: Hudhayfah, alarmed by differences in recitation, came to Uthman.

t: The sheets of the Qur'an were kept with Hafsah before Uthman's copies.
f: The sheets of the Qur'an were kept with Aishah before Uthman's copies.
x: After Abu Bakr and Umar, the sheets stayed with Hafsah.

t: Hafs narrated the recitation of 'Asim.
f: Hafs narrated the recitation of Nafi'.
x: Hafs is 'Asim's narrator. Warsh and Qalun narrate from Nafi'.

t: Ayat al-Dayn is the longest verse in the Qur'an.
f: Ayat al-Kursi is the longest verse in the Qur'an.
x: The verse of debt, Al-Baqarah 282, is the longest.

t: Surah An-Naml contains a basmalah in the middle of the surah.
f: Surah Al-Kahf contains a basmalah in the middle of the surah.
x: Sulayman's letter in Surah An-Naml begins with the basmalah.

t: Surah Al-Mujadilah mentions the name of Allah in every verse.
f: Surah Al-Kawthar mentions the name of Allah in every verse.
x: Al-Mujadilah is known for mentioning Allah in every one of its verses. Al-Kawthar does not name Allah.

t: Zayd is named in Surah Al-Ahzab.
f: Zayd is named in Surah Al-Baqarah.
x: Al-Ahzab 37 names Zayd.

t: Ahmad, as a name of the Prophet ﷺ, appears in Surah As-Saff.
f: Ahmad, as a name of the Prophet ﷺ, appears in Surah Al-Fatihah.
x: Isa gave good news of a messenger "whose name is Ahmad".

t: The name Muhammad appears four times in the Qur'an.
f: The name Muhammad appears forty times in the Qur'an.
x: It appears in Ali 'Imran, Al-Ahzab, Muhammad and Al-Fath.

t: Idris is named twice in the Qur'an.
f: Idris is named twenty times in the Qur'an.
x: Idris is named in Maryam and Al-Anbiya.

t: Musa is the prophet named most often in the Qur'an.
f: Yunus is the prophet named most often in the Qur'an.
x: Musa is named more than any other prophet.

t: Twenty-five prophets are named in the Qur'an.
f: Seventy prophets are named in the Qur'an.
x: Twenty-five prophets and messengers are named.

t: The People of the Ditch are mentioned in Surah Al-Buruj.
f: The People of the Ditch are mentioned in Surah Al-Fil.
x: Surah Al-Buruj mentions the makers of the ditch.

t: The flood of 'Arim destroyed the gardens of Saba'.
f: The flood of 'Arim destroyed the people of Lut.
x: Allah sent upon Saba' the flood of al-'Arim.

t: Talut tested his army by forbidding them to drink from a river.
f: Talut tested his army by forbidding them to eat dates.
x: Those who drank from the river beyond a handful were not of him.

t: The man who died for a hundred years found his food unspoiled.
f: The man who died for a hundred years found his donkey still alive and young.
x: His food and drink had not changed, but his donkey had turned to bones.

t: The People of the Sabbath were turned into apes.
f: The People of the Sabbath were turned into stone.
x: Allah said to them, "Be apes, despised."

t: The believer of Fir'awn's family hid his faith.
f: The believer of Fir'awn's family was Haman.
x: Surah Ghafir describes a believer from Fir'awn's family who concealed his faith.

t: Al-Samiri made the golden calf.
f: Harun made the golden calf.
x: Al-Samiri made the calf. Harun tried to stop the people.

t: Dhul-Qarnayn travelled to where the sun sets and where it rises.
f: Dhul-Qarnayn stayed in one city all his life.
x: Al-Kahf describes his journeys west and east.

t: Al-Khidr rebuilt a falling wall without asking for payment.
f: Al-Khidr demanded payment for rebuilding a wall.
x: Musa suggested payment, but al-Khidr repaired it freely for two orphans.

t: The Qur'an calls Ibrahim "Khalil", the intimate friend of Allah.
f: The Qur'an calls Nuh "Khalil", the intimate friend of Allah.
x: Allah took Ibrahim as a close friend.

t: Musa is called Kalimullah because Allah spoke to him directly.
f: Isa is called Kalimullah because Allah spoke to him on Mount Sinai.
x: Allah spoke to Musa directly.

t: Isa spoke as a baby in the cradle.
f: Yahya spoke as a baby in the cradle to defend his mother.
x: Isa spoke from the cradle to defend Maryam.

t: The Battle of Yamamah was fought against Musaylimah.
f: The Battle of Yamamah was fought against the Byzantines.
x: Yamamah was fought against the false prophet Musaylimah.

t: Abu Bakr's caliphate lasted about two years.
f: Abu Bakr's caliphate lasted about twenty years.
x: He ruled from 11 to 13 AH.

t: Umar's caliphate lasted about ten years.
f: Umar's caliphate lasted about one year.
x: Umar ruled from 13 to 23 AH.

t: Umar was stabbed while leading the prayer in the mosque.
f: Umar was killed in the Battle of Yarmuk.
x: Umar was stabbed in Madinah just after starting the prayer as imam.

t: Umar appointed six men to choose the next caliph.
f: Umar appointed his son as the next caliph.
x: Umar named six of the companions as a council.

t: Uthman was martyred in his house in Madinah.
f: Uthman was martyred at Siffin.
x: Uthman was killed by rebels in his house in 35 AH.

t: The Battle of the Camel was fought near Basra.
f: The Battle of the Camel was fought near Makkah.
x: The Camel (36 AH) was fought near Basra.

t: Ammar ibn Yasir was killed at Siffin.
f: Ammar ibn Yasir was killed at Badr.
x: Ammar was killed at Siffin in 37 AH.

t: The Hijri calendar was adopted under Umar.
f: The Hijri calendar was adopted under Uthman.
x: Umar adopted the dating from the Hijrah.

t: Umar set Dhat 'Irq as the miqat for Iraq.
f: The Prophet ﷺ set Dhat 'Irq as the miqat for Egypt.
x: Umar fixed Dhat 'Irq for the people of Iraq.

t: The plague of Amwas struck al-Sham in Umar's time.
f: The plague of Amwas struck Makkah in Abu Bakr's time.
x: It struck al-Sham around 18 AH, and Abu Ubaydah died in it.

t: The Umayyad capital was Damascus.
f: The Umayyad capital was Baghdad.
x: The Umayyads ruled from Damascus. Baghdad was the Abbasid capital.

t: Baghdad was founded by the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur.
f: Baghdad was founded by Umar ibn al-Khattab.
x: Al-Mansur founded Baghdad in 145 AH.

t: The Mongols sacked Baghdad in 656 AH.
f: The Mongols sacked Baghdad in 156 AH.
x: Baghdad fell to the Mongols in 656 AH.

t: Salah al-Din retook Jerusalem after the Battle of Hattin.
f: Salah al-Din retook Jerusalem after the Battle of Badr.
x: Hattin opened the way to Jerusalem in 583 AH.

t: The Battle of Ain Jalut was fought against the Mongols.
f: The Battle of Ain Jalut was fought against the Byzantines.
x: The Mamluks defeated the Mongols at Ain Jalut in 658 AH.

t: Granada was the last Muslim kingdom in al-Andalus.
f: Cordoba was the last Muslim kingdom in al-Andalus to fall.
x: Granada fell last, in 897 AH.

t: The Dome of the Rock was built under Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan.
f: The Dome of the Rock was built under Harun al-Rashid.
x: Abd al-Malik built it, completed in 72 AH.

t: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz ruled for about two and a half years.
f: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz ruled for about forty years.
x: He ruled from 99 to 101 AH.

t: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari is buried near Constantinople.
f: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari is buried in Yemen.
x: He died on the expedition to Constantinople and was buried near its walls.

t: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas commanded the Muslims at Qadisiyyah.
f: Khalid ibn al-Walid commanded the Muslims at Qadisiyyah.
x: Sa'd led the army at Qadisiyyah. Khalid had been sent to al-Sham.

t: The siege of Ta'if came after the Battle of Hunayn.
f: The siege of Ta'if came before the Battle of Badr.
x: After Hunayn in 8 AH the Muslims besieged Ta'if.

t: Banu Qaynuqa' were the first Jewish tribe expelled from Madinah.
f: Banu Qurayzah were the first Jewish tribe expelled from Madinah.
x: Qaynuqa' were expelled after Badr, Banu al-Nadir after Uhud.

t: Surah Al-Hashr was revealed about Banu al-Nadir.
f: Surah Al-Hashr was revealed about Abu Lahab.
x: Ibn Abbas called Al-Hashr the surah of Banu al-Nadir.

t: The incident of the Ifk happened on the return from Banu al-Mustaliq.
f: The incident of the Ifk happened on the return from Tabuk.
x: Aishah was left behind looking for her necklace on the return from that expedition.

t: Seventy reciters were killed at Bi'r Ma'unah.
f: Seven hundred reciters were killed at Bi'r Ma'unah.
x: The Prophet ﷺ sent seventy reciters, who were betrayed and killed.

t: The Prophet ﷺ made qunut against the killers of the reciters for a month.
f: The Prophet ﷺ made qunut against the killers of the reciters for ten years.
x: He supplicated against them in qunut for a month.

t: Abdullah ibn Ubayy withdrew about a third of the army before Uhud.
f: Abdullah ibn Ubayy led the archers at Uhud.
x: He turned back with about a third of the army. The archers were led by Abdullah ibn Jubayr.

t: Ka'b ibn Malik was one of the three who stayed behind from Tabuk.
f: Ka'b ibn Malik led the army to Tabuk.
x: Ka'b told the story of how he stayed behind and was forgiven.

t: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh judged the case of Banu Qurayzah.
f: Abu Bakr judged the case of Banu Qurayzah.
x: The Prophet ﷺ appointed Sa'd ibn Mu'adh to judge.

t: Thumamah ibn Uthal was tied to a pillar of the mosque before accepting Islam.
f: Thumamah ibn Uthal was a companion from Makkah who migrated to Abyssinia.
x: Thumamah, a chief of al-Yamamah, was held in the mosque and then accepted Islam.

t: Abdullah ibn Salam was a Jewish scholar of Madinah before Islam.
f: Abdullah ibn Salam was a Persian priest before Islam.
x: He was a learned rabbi of Madinah.

t: Safiyyah's dowry was her freedom.
f: Safiyyah's dowry was a garden in Khaybar.
x: The Prophet ﷺ freed her and made that her dowry.

t: Juwayriyah's people were freed after her marriage to the Prophet ﷺ.
f: Juwayriyah was the daughter of the chief of Quraysh.
x: She was the daughter of the chief of Banu al-Mustaliq.

t: Sawdah gave her day to Aishah.
f: Aishah gave her day to Sawdah.
x: Sawdah gave her turn to Aishah.

t: Hafsah was the daughter of Umar.
f: Hafsah was the daughter of Abu Bakr.
x: Hafsah was Umar's daughter. Aishah was Abu Bakr's.

t: Zaynab bint Jahsh was previously married to Zayd ibn Harithah.
f: Zaynab bint Jahsh was previously married to Abu Lahab.
x: Al-Ahzab 37 refers to Zayd's divorce of her and her marriage to the Prophet ﷺ.

t: Asma bint Abi Bakr is called the one with two waistbands.
f: Fatimah is called the one with two waistbands.
x: Asma tore her waistband in two for the Hijrah provisions.

t: The Prophet ﷺ was shrouded in three white cloths.
f: The Prophet ﷺ was shrouded in seven green cloths.
x: Aishah said three white Yemeni sheets.

t: The Prophet's ring was engraved "Muhammad Messenger of Allah".
f: The Prophet's ring was engraved with his date of birth.
x: He had a silver ring engraved Muhammad Rasul Allah.

t: The Prophet's she-camel al-Qaswa' knelt at Hudaybiyyah.
f: The Prophet's she-camel al-Qaswa' knelt at Badr and refused to fight.
x: Al-Qaswa' knelt at Hudaybiyyah.

t: Al-Buraq was the mount of the Night Journey.
f: Al-Qaswa' was the mount of the Night Journey.
x: The Prophet ﷺ rode al-Buraq on the Isra.

t: Seventy thousand angels enter al-Bayt al-Ma'mur every day.
f: Seven angels enter al-Bayt al-Ma'mur every year.
x: The Prophet ﷺ was told seventy thousand angels pray in it daily.

t: The Prophet ﷺ met Ibrahim in the seventh heaven on the Mi'raj.
f: The Prophet ﷺ met Ibrahim in the first heaven on the Mi'raj.
x: He met Adam in the first heaven and Ibrahim in the seventh.

t: The prayers were first prescribed as fifty and reduced to five.
f: The prayers were first prescribed as three and increased to five.
x: On Musa's advice the Prophet ﷺ asked for a reduction until they became five.

t: Kalalah is someone who leaves neither parent nor child.
f: Kalalah is someone who leaves only a son.
x: The last verse of An-Nisa concerns kalalah, the one without parent or child.

t: The Qur'an gives the husband four months in the case of ila'.
f: The Qur'an gives the husband four years in the case of ila'.
x: Al-Baqarah 226: a wait of four months.

t: The expiation for zihar includes fasting two consecutive months.
f: The expiation for zihar is fasting one day.
x: Al-Mujadilah: free a slave, or fast two consecutive months, or feed sixty needy.

t: In li'an each spouse swears four times and then a fifth oath.
f: In li'an each spouse swears once.
x: Surah An-Nur: four testimonies, then a fifth invoking curse or wrath.

t: A widow's waiting period is four months and ten days.
f: A widow's waiting period is three days.
x: Al-Baqarah 234 sets four months and ten days.

t: A bequest is limited to a third of the estate.
f: A bequest may cover the whole estate even with heirs.
x: The Prophet ﷺ told Sa'd, "A third, and a third is much."

t: A fifth of the spoils is set aside in Surah Al-Anfal.
f: Half of the spoils is set aside in Surah Al-Anfal.
x: Al-Anfal 41 sets aside a fifth.

t: Expiation for a broken oath can be feeding ten poor people.
f: Expiation for a broken oath is feeding one hundred poor people.
x: Al-Ma'idah 89 names feeding ten needy people.

t: Days of Tashriq are the 11th, 12th and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah.
f: Days of Tashriq are the first three days of Shawwal.
x: They are the three days after the Day of Sacrifice.

t: The white days are the 13th, 14th and 15th of the lunar month.
f: The white days are the 1st, 2nd and 3rd of the lunar month.
x: The Prophet ﷺ advised fasting the 13th, 14th and 15th.

t: The miqat for the people of al-Sham is al-Juhfah.
f: The miqat for the people of al-Sham is Yalamlam.
x: Al-Juhfah is for al-Sham. Yalamlam is for Yemen.

t: Qarn al-Manazil is the miqat for the people of Najd.
f: Qarn al-Manazil is the miqat for the people of Madinah.
x: Qarn is for Najd. Dhul-Hulayfah is for Madinah.

t: The Prophet ﷺ performed four umrahs.
f: The Prophet ﷺ performed forty umrahs.
x: Anas said four umrahs.

t: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for those who shave their heads three times in Hajj.
f: The Prophet ﷺ forbade shaving the head in Hajj.
x: He prayed for those who shave, then included those who trim.

t: Umar turned back from al-Sham because of the plague.
f: Umar entered al-Sham during the plague to lead the prayer there.
x: On hearing the Prophet's instruction he returned.

t: The Throne shook at the death of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh.
f: The Throne shook at the death of Abu Lahab.
x: The Prophet ﷺ said the Throne shook for Sa'd ibn Mu'adh.

t: Abu Dharr's name was Jundub ibn Junadah.
f: Abu Dharr's name was Abd al-Rahman ibn Sakhr.
x: Abu Dharr was Jundub ibn Junadah. Abd al-Rahman ibn Sakhr is a name given for Abu Hurayrah.

t: Salman al-Farisi came from Persia.
f: Salman al-Farisi came from Abyssinia.
x: Salman was Persian. Bilal's family came from Abyssinia.

t: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari came from Yemen.
f: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari came from Persia.
x: He was of the Ash'ari tribe of Yemen.
